synthesis:draft.headline: POE50 forecasts for VIC1 were on average −183.96 MW (mean error) with MAE 186.88 MW over 2026-07-28 15:30 AEST–2026-07-29 03:30 AEST.
summary: The forecast-vs-actual comparison used 24 paired half-hour intervals for VIC1 (2026-07-28T05:30:00Z–2026-07-28T17:30:00Z) (ev0630).
Mean error (POE50 − actual) = −183.96 MW (ev0629) and mean absolute error (MAE) = 186.88 MW (ev0628).
The single largest absolute error in the window was −508.0 MW at interval ending 2026-07-28T06:30:00Z (ev0538).
The highest observed actual operational demand in the review window was 7995.0 MW at interval ending 2026-07-28T09:00:00Z (ev0514).
Many intervals had much smaller signed errors (examples: +14.0 MW at 2026-07-28T15:00:00Z (ev0606), +10.0 MW at 2026-07-28T15:30:00Z (ev0610), +11.0 MW at 2026-07-28T16:00:00Z (ev0614)).

possible_explanations.statement: The POE50 forecasts may have been systematically lower than actual demand during the review window, as shown by the negative mean error (ev0629) and MAE (ev0628).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare runs issued at different available times such as 2026-07-28T05:18:24Z, 2026-07-28T05:48:22Z and 2026-07-28T06:18:23Z (run available_at_utc values shown in the compare output) to see whether later runs reduced the negative bias.

possible_explanations.statement: The bias might be related to demand drivers (for example, weather deviations) that differed from inputs used by the forecast model.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare interval-level weather observations and forecast inputs for intervals such as 2026-07-28T06:30:00Z and 2026-07-28T09:00:00Z (times returned in the compare output) against the forecast inputs used for the matching runs.

possible_explanations.statement: Model input or data-assimilation issues for specific morning intervals could have produced the large underestimates (for example the −508.0 MW error at 2026-07-28T06:30:00Z, ev0538).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Inspect the individual run metadata and preceding runs for the interval ending 2026-07-28T06:30:00Z (the compare output lists run_ids and run issued/available times such as those with available_at_utc around 2026-07-28T05:48:22Z) to see whether inputs or run timing differ for that interval.
